summary:
Since the 1960s, NASA has left historic hardware across the Moon and Mars—from Apollo descent stages to rovers and helicopters. While these machines enabled groundbreaking discoveries, traditional science articles often feel too technical for school-age learners, leaving their stories overlooked.

Abandoned, Not Forgotten: The Silent Explorers of Space(Voices of the Void) is an interactive AI-powered web application and digital storytelling experience designed for young space enthusiasts. Using conversational AI built via Google AI Studio and Gemini, users can talk directly in real-time with simulated personas of four iconic NASA artifacts: the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Apollo Retroreflector Arrays, the Opportunity rover, and the Ingenuity Mars helicopter. Grounded in official NASA mission archives, our solution turns complex planetary science into an engaging, accessible conversation that inspires the next generation of explorers.
details:
Our project is an interactive, conversational web application built for school-age students (ages 8–14) to explore space history. Instead of reading static encyclopedia entries, users interact with a sci-fi chat interface where they can ask questions and talk directly with AI-simulated personas of retired NASA hardware on the Moon and Mars.

How It Works & Tools Used: The application was developed using Google AI Studio and Gemini 1.5 Flash, utilizing custom System Instructions to ground the AI's responses in authentic NASA telemetry, engineering specs, and mission logs. The front-end interface was exported from Google AI Studio and deployed live via Netlify.

Impact & Creativity: By giving silent machines a relatable voice and anchoring every response in real discoveries—such as lunar laser ranging and Martian water-formed minerals—our project sparks curiosity in STEM and brings humanity's off-world heritage to life.
